description: O11 (EDIT coverage on a STATIC ENTITY): maintain a static entity that THIS job did not create. The base is job:spec-data, so the Status with its Active/Inactive records, the Contact whose StatusId has type 'Status Identifier' and default Entities.Status.Active, the filter 'Contact.StatusId = Entities.Status.Active' in Contact_CountActive and the ContactSummary already exist when the first op runs - there is no creation op here, on purpose: creating and editing in the same job proves no maintenance at all. Outside the job that created them there are no aliases: the entity is cited as 'IStaticEntity:Status', a record as 'IStaticEntity:Status/Active' and the value of a column in that record as 'IStaticEntity:Status/Active/Label' - three levels. WHAT THIS JOB PINS DOWN IN THE O11 LANE, measured: (A) the record is an OutSystems.Model.Data.IRecord (class ServiceStudio.Model.StaticRecord) and does NOT publish Name - the get shows Identifier, and the rename op writes that same Identifier (tests/jobs/rename-name-property.json; until 2026-10-03 it refused with "IRecord 'Active' has no Name"). The native path is 'set Identifier', and the kernel pre-checks the clash (tests/jobs-negative/set-identifier-clash.json). (B) writing Identifier is NOT a label: the two real consumers of the record (the DefaultValue of StatusId and the aggregate filter) are rewritten by the platform from Entities.Status.Active to Entities.Status.Open without a single op touching them, and usages keeps returning the SAME two consumers (count 2, real 2) before and after. (C) the value of the record's Label column ALSO follows, but only when it is exactly the quotes around the old name: Active had Label "Active" and becomes "Open" on its own; Inactive gets Label "Not active" BEFORE, is renamed Closed and the Label stays "Not active" - only by hand does it become "Closed". It is the same rule the ODC lane proves in tests/jobs-odc/static-entity-lifecycle.json, now measured in SS11. (D) the ENTITY has Name and is renamed with the rename op (consumers 3, expressionsRewritten 2): the default becomes Entities.ContactStatus.Open, the filter too, the anonymous 'Status Record' becomes 'ContactStatus Record', GetStatus becomes GetContactStatus and the type 'Status Identifier' becomes 'ContactStatus Identifier' - and the find for 'Status' only returns the homonymous attribute of ContactSummary, which is another author's text. (E) the dump lists the records in an order that is neither the creation order nor that of Order and does not even repeat from run to run (measured: in one run Inactive before Active, in the next Active before Inactive): IStaticEntity.Records is an IEnumerable and not a sequence with author order, which is the reason for the refusal of move in tests/jobs-negative/move-static-record.json. The ObjectKeys also change from run to run (the base is reapplied each time), so the _why texts say 'the same key' and never cite one.

ops.name: Status
ops._why: (0) the starting point is INHERITED from job:spec-data: three objects answer to Status - the IStaticEntity, the IStructureAttribute Status of the ContactSummary (another author's text, which will not follow anything) and the IAttribute Status of the 'Status Record', the anonymous structure the platform generated with the entity. The find (13f) makes this list again after the entity rename and only the structure attribute survives with this name.

(1) BEFORE, the entity: EntityKind Static, Attributes 3, Records 2, Description null, Label 'Status', LabelPlural 'Statuses', LabelAttribute pointing at the Label column. This is the column branch (C) will watch. Keep the entity's ObjectKey: the get (14b) must bring the same one.

(2) BEFORE, the tree: 3 IEntityAttribute (Id, Label, Order), 2 IRecord (iface OutSystems.Model.Data.IRecord, class ServiceStudio.Model.StaticRecord) each with 3 IRecordAttributeValue and the value in an IExpression ("Active"/1, "Inactive"/2; the Id one without text), plus the generated GetStatus and 'Status Identifier'. NOTE the order of the records: it is not the creation order (the spec created Active first) nor that of Order (1, 2), and it changes from run to run (measured Inactive/Active in one and Active/Inactive in another) - Records is an IEnumerable, with no author sequence, and that is why move is refused on this type. It is the snapshot the dump (15) is compared with.

(3) BEFORE, the first real consumer, inherited: DataType is the key of the 'Status Identifier' and DefaultValue is 'Entities.Status.Active'. No op of this job writes this text - whatever happens to it, the platform did it.

(4) BEFORE, who holds the Active record: count 2, real 2, both IExpression and none derived - the filter 'Contact.StatusId = Entities.Status.Active' (IServerAction:Contact_CountActive/IAggregateNode:GetActive/DataTable/ICombineSourcesOperation:Contacts/IFilter/IExpression) and the DefaultValue of StatusId (IServerEntity:Contact/IEntityAttribute:StatusId/IExpression). These are the two that (11f) must return with the same keys and different text.

(5) BEFORE, who holds the ENTITY: count 3, real 3 - the same two expressions plus the IAttribute Status of the 'Status Record' (IAnonymousStructure:Status Record/IAttribute:Status). Baseline for usages (13d).

(6) BEFORE, the record up close: Identifier = Active, AttributeValues 3 and NO Name property - which is why the rename op refuses on this type and why (11a) writes Identifier. The get (11b) must bring the same ObjectKey, otherwise there was a recreation and not an edit.

(7) BEFORE, the value that decides branch (C): IRecordAttributeValue with Attribute = Label and Value = "Active", exactly the record name in quotes. The get (11e) reads the same wrapper with other text inside.
(8) BEFORE, the second consumer in writing: the IFilter of the aggregate GetActive has the Condition 'Contact.StatusId = Entities.Status.Active'. (11d) and (13c) are read against this dump.

ops.name: Pending
ops._why: (9a) CHANGE 1 - add a record to an INHERITED static entity. The parent is a path and not an $alias, because another job declared the entity. An OutSystems.Model.Data.IRecord is born with 3 empty IRecordAttributeValue, one per inherited column.
a static entity never has an AutoNumber Id: the new record gets its Id, the one after those of the spec (Active 1, Inactive 2).
the Value is an expression (via SetValue), so the text carries the OutSystems quotes inside the JSON quotes. $p/<Attribute> reaches the value of that column in this record.
after the two inherited ones (1, 2): the OrderByAttribute rules the read order and the new record enters that sequence by hand.
(9b) AFTER: Identifier = Pending, AttributeValues 3, and again no Name. The $p alias exists only because THIS job created it.
the value read back: Attribute = the same Label column of the inherited records and Value "Pending".
(9c) Records went from 2 to 3 and Attributes is still 3: adding a record does not touch the schema. Compare with the get (1).
(9d) count 0, real 0: a record is born without consumers even in an entity that already has two. It is the reading that static-record-refactor.json will contradict later after the replace.

(10a) BEFORE arming the no-propagation branch: Inactive has Label "Inactive", equal to the name in quotes - if it stayed like that, (12a) would rewrite it as it will rewrite Active's. Keep the key of this IRecordAttributeValue: the get (12b) reads the same one by another path.

(10b) THE TRAP, ON PURPOSE: a Label written by an author that is NOT the record name. It is what separates (12b) from (11e): two sibling records, the same operation, opposite results. The target is written as 'IRecord:Inactive/Label' (type:record name, searched in the whole module) and not as 'IStaticEntity:Status/Inactive/Label', on purpose: the data contract stores the write to a record value as '@<key of the first segment>/<rest of the path>' and resolves the rest BY NAME again at the end of the job. With the three-level path the assertion would be '@<entity key>/Inactive/Label' and, after (12a) changes the Identifier to Closed, the end of the job failed with "IStaticEntity 'ContactStatus' has no child 'Inactive'" (measured). With the record in the first segment the assertion is '@<record key>/Label' and it survives the rename. It is the only way to write the Label of an inherited record that is going to change its name in the same job.

(11a) CHANGE 2 - rename an inherited record by the NATIVE path of the O11 lane: IRecord.Identifier is the writable property of the name (via 'property'). The rename op does the same, through the same property (tests/jobs/rename-name-property.json). The kernel pre-checks the clash: 'set Identifier: ... clashes with an existing name in that scope' (tests/jobs-negative/set-identifier-clash.json), instead of letting the Studio add a suffix silently.
(11b) AFTER: Identifier = Open and the SAME ObjectKey as get (6) - no record was born. The path already resolves by /Open.

(11c) THE CENTRAL PROOF, first half: the inherited DefaultValue already says 'Entities.Status.Open' with no hand correction (it was 'Entities.Status.Active' in get (3)). The expression is linked to the IRecord by key and the platform regenerated the text when the Identifier changed.

(11d) the second consumer too: the Condition of the IFilter now says 'Contact.StatusId = Entities.Status.Open' (it was Active in dump (8)). Writing Identifier is not a label shortcut: if it were, both expressions would still say Active and the module would fall at Verify.

(11e) THE BRANCH WITH PROPAGATION, measured in SS11: the same wrapper (same ObjectKey) as get (7), and the Value went from "Active" to "Open" ON ITS OWN. The value of the Label column was exactly the quotes around the old name, so the platform swapped it. Compare with (12b).

(11f) count 2, real 2 - the SAME two consumer keys as usages (4) (<IFilter key>.#Condition and <StatusId key>.#DefaultValue), with the text already rewritten ('Contact.StatusId = Entities.Status.Open' and 'Entities.Status.Open'). Changing the name did not release anyone.

ops.name: Active
ops._why: (11g) EMPTY list: nothing in the module answers to Active - neither the record (now Open) nor the Label (carried by the propagation branch). It settles the question of whether Identifier was a second field next to the name.

(12a) CHANGE 3 - the same verb as (11a) on the sibling record, whose Label stopped being equal to the name in (10b). No consumers (no expression cites Inactive), so the only thing that can follow is the Label.

(12b) THE BRANCH WITHOUT PROPAGATION, measured: the Value is still "Not active", in the SAME IRecordAttributeValue as get (10a) - the three-level path and 'IRecord:Name/Label' reach the same wrapper. The platform only swaps the Label when it is exactly "<OldName>"; "Not active" was never "Inactive", so it stayed. Next to (11e), the whole rule fits in the comparison of one string.

(12c) the hand correction of what (12b) showed does not follow: the content of the Label column IN THIS record, the text the user reads in a dropdown. Same target shape as (10b), for the same reason: the entity is still going to change its name in (13a), and the contract assertion must stay tied to the record key. As (10b) and this op write the SAME assertion ('@<record key>/Label', property Value), the contract keeps only the last one: "Closed".
(12d) AFTER: Value "Closed", the same wrapper as get (10a) and (12b) - the value was rewritten in place, no new wrapper was born.

ops.name: ContactStatus
ops._why: (13a) CHANGE 4 - rename the inherited ENTITY ITSELF, with two real consumers linked and two records already renamed inside. Here the rename op WORKS, because IStaticEntity publishes Name: it is the direct contrast with (11a). It returns consumers 3 and expressionsRewritten 2 - the two expressions; the third consumer is the IAttribute of the 'Status Record', which follows by key and has no text to rewrite.

(13b) THE CENTRAL PROOF, second half: the DefaultValue now says 'Entities.ContactStatus.Open' - BOTH parts of the citation were rewritten, each by its own verb (set Identifier and rename), neither by this job. The DataType is the same key, because the identifier type is generated by the entity. The attribute is still called StatusId and its Label 'Status': author names do not follow.

(13c) the filter says 'Contact.StatusId = Entities.ContactStatus.Open'. Third reading of the same Condition (the same key <IFilter key>.#Condition): Active -> Open -> ContactStatus.Open, and the job never wrote it.

(13d) compare with usages (5): the SAME three consumer keys (count 3, real 3), with the new names in the texts and the path of the anonymous attribute already at 'IAnonymousStructure:ContactStatus Record/IAttribute:ContactStatus'. Consumers stay linked by key; that is why rename rewrites the text without losing anyone.
(13e) the renamed record seen through the new path of the entity: the same 2 real consumers as (4) and (11f).

ops.name: Status
ops._why: (13f) compare with the find (0): of the three objects only the IStructureAttribute Status of the ContactSummary remains - another author's text, which no rename touches. The entity and the 'Status Record' disappeared together, because the second is generated FROM the entity.

ops.name: ContactStatus
ops._why: (13g) and here is where they reappear with the new name: the IStaticEntity and the IAttribute of the 'ContactStatus Record', without a single op asking for it.

ops.value: Estado de um contacto. O valor por omissao de Contact.StatusId e Entities.ContactStatus.Open.
ops._why: (14a) author write on the inherited top-level element, AFTER the renames on purpose: written before, it cited dead names and nothing fixed it. The data contract reads it back word for word.

(14b) AFTER, the entity: compare with the get (1). The Name, the Label ('Contact Status') and the LabelPlural ('Contact Statuses') CHANGED, derived from the name; the Description is the one from (14a); Records is 3. The ObjectKey of the get (1), the EntityKind Static and the Identifier/Label/OrderBy pointing at the same attributes STAYED.

(15) the final tree, next to dump (2): the 3 attributes with the same keys, 3 IRecord instead of 2 - Closed (was Inactive, Label "Closed" set by an AUTHOR), Open (was Active, Label "Open" set by the PLATFORM) and Pending, in an order that again is not the creation order (measured Pending, Open, Closed) -, the entity action already GetContactStatus and the type already 'ContactStatus Identifier'. What the platform redid is all here; what was left to the author is too.
